08/ 19.06.2023

This petition has been filed for quashing of the entire criminal proceedings
including the order taking cognizance dated 20.04.2015, by which, cognizance for the offence under
Sections 409, 420 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code has been taken against the petitioner, in
connection with learned Judicial Magistrate, Koderma.
2.  Mr. Anil Kumar Sinha, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the matter is still pending for framing of charge.
He submits that the learned court has taken the cognizance against the petitioner without any materials available on record.

He further submits that earlier the learned Court has also taken the cognizance, which was set aside by this court and referred back to the learned concerned court to pass a fresh order on the point of cognizance.
He further submits that again the same mistake has been committed by the learned court by taking cognizance against the petitioner.
He further submits that the petitioner has not been sent up for trial, however, the learned court without differing with the final form has taken the cognizance.
On these grounds, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that this petition is fit to be allowed.
3. Mr. Suraj Deo Munda, learned A.P.P. appearing for the State submits that at least in one of the paragraph of the case diary the name of the petitioner has come.
He submits that at this stage, this court may not interfere in the matter.

sentences.text:
In view of the above submissions of the parties, it appears that the points advanced in the argument of learned counsel appearing for the petitioner are fit to be considered at the time of framing of charge and in that view of the matter Mr. Sinha, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner, on instruction, seeks permission to withdraw this petition with the liberty to file the discharge petition at the appropriate stage.
5.
Learned A.P.P. appearing for the State has got no objection.
6. This petition is permitted to be withdrawn and disposed of with the aforesaid liberty.

(Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) Amitesh/-
